 Mike Snider, USA TODAY Updated Fri, November 20, 2026 at 7:17 PM UTC 3 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. The Food and Drug Administration has expanded a recall of certain food products sold at workplaces and in vending machines for possible listeria contamination.
 Grand Strand Sandwich Company Inc., of Longs, South Carolina, is recalling several of its Lunch Box sandwiches, distributed between March 2 and Nov. 10, in clear plastic packaging and sold primarily in retail convenience stores, vending machines and prison canteens, located in North Carolina, South Carolina and Virginia, the company said in an alert on the FDA website .
 Grand Strand said it was notified on Nov. 11 that biscuits supplied by Dot Foods may be contaminated with the disease-causing bacteria Listeria monocytogenes . Dot Foods , of Mt. Sterling, Illinois, has a distribution relationship with grain-based and frozen food producer C.H. Guenther of San Antonio, Texas; biscuits made by C.H. Guenther & Son have been part of a Nov. 14 recall issued by the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS).
 Consumer Reports , the nonprofit known for testing and monitoring consumer-facing policy and products, released its annual risky food report in April, naming the 10 foods of 2024 that were subject to the most recalls and/or associated with the largest illness outbreaks. USA TODAY broke it down further on a what-you-need-to-know basis. 
 (Joe Raedle, Getty Images) Deli meat is somewhat of a "risky" food as it is often associated with the spread of listeria, such as in the 2024 case of the Boar's Head listeria outbreak that killed 10. Listeria monocytogenes is a hardy germ that can survive in very low temperatures but thrives in cool and damp places. It can, and will, happily live on foods in your or your grocery store's storage area, and the process for mass-producing the meat lends itself to plenty of opportunities for contamination.
 (Lauri Patterson, Getty Images) Produce, like the cucumbers recalled due to a salmonella  outbreak that infected 113 people across 23 states, can become adulterated with harmful bacteria through fecal contamination, which can occur through wastewater, water in the growing area, fertilizer and the proximity of the growing area to livestock.
 (Getty Images) Raw dairy, which is always unsafe to consume and illegal to sell in some states, poses a risk when it's not pasteurized. Dairy pasteurization, or heating milk products to a high enough temperature to kill harmful bacteria, has been practiced since the 1920s. (RA Simon, Getty Images) Cotija and queso fresco cheese are made from unpasteurized milk, meaning they carry an increased risk. One producer, Rizo-Lopez Foods, was shut down in October 2024 after its cheeses were linked to a years-long listeria outbreak that killed two people and made dozens of others sick.
 (Marcos Elihu Castillo Ramirez, Getty Images) Eggs can become contaminated via the same means as cucumbers and other raw produce, especially if they have a cracked shell. 
 (Getty Images) Like other raw produce, onions can become infected via fecal contamination. In 2024, E. coli-contaminated slivered onions on McDonald's Quarter Pounders triggered some locations to stop serving the burger temporarily. 
 (iStockphoto, Getty Images) Like cucumbers and onions, leafy greens are easily contaminated with bacteria like E. coli, as in the case of the Solata Foods spinach recall in 2024. 
 (Edalin, Getty Images) Organic carrots were linked to a major E. coli outbreak in late 2024, leaving at least 39 ill and one dead. 
 (Hyrma, Getty Images) Ready-to-eat/cooked poultry and meat have been the source of multiple major recalls and foodborne illness outbreaks in recent years. The same issue arises with RTE foods as with deli meat; the conditions they are made and stored under are often ideal for bacteria such as listeria to grow. In 2024, millions of pounds of RTE foods were recalled by BrucePac for listeria contamination. 
 (Getty Images) See the 'risky foods' linked to US recalls and illness outbreaks

 Which products were recalled?
 Grand Strand Sandwich Company said the following products – sold primarily in retail convenience stores, vending machines and prison canteens, located in North Carolina, South Carolina and Virginia – were voluntarily recalled. No illnesses have been reported to date.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Lunch Box Bacon Egg and Cheese Biscuit, 4-ounce: UPC 0 67068 21400 8
 Lunch Box Chicken Sausage Biscuit, 3.75-ounce: UPC 0 67068 21404 6
 Lunch Box Jumbo Sausage Biscuit, 4-ounce: UPC 0 67068 21407 7
 Lunch Box Sausage Egg & Cheese Biscuit, 5-ounce: UPC 0 67068 21402 2
 Grand Strand Sandwich Company Inc. of Longs, S.C. is recalling several Lunch Box ready-to-eat sandwiches including the Lunch Box Bacon Egg and Cheese Biscuit and Lunch Box Chicken Sausage Biscuit for possible listeria contamination. Consumers who purchased these products are urged to return them to the place of purchase for a full refund, or discard the product. Consumers with questions may contact Grand Strand Sandwich at 843-399-2999 Monday-Thursday from 8 a.m. - 4 p.m. ET, and Friday 8 a.m. to Noon ET.
 Related products recalled: 
 Several other ready-to-eat products with biscuits made by C.H. Guenther & Son were recently recalled for potential listeria contamination, according to the FDA and USDA.
 Advertisement Advertisement Mmm! Meals Made in Minutes Biscuit & Sausage Gravy ready-to-eat biscuit sandwiches sold in vending machines in six states, including Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Oklahoma, Tennessee and Texas (bestby dates of Nov. 12-18).
 Fresh to You Sausage, Egg & Cheese Biscuit Sandwich distributed in break rooms, refrigerated vending machines and cafeterias, as part of the larger biscuit recall. These were sold in Alabama, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Oklahoma, Tennessee and Texas (best-by dates of Nov. 7-19).
 Fresh to You Sausage, Egg & Cheese Biscuit Sandwiches sold in Oregon and Washington between Oct. 25 and Nov. 4 were largely distributed to employee break rooms, refrigerated vending machines and cafeterias (best-by dates of Nov. 7-19).

 What are the symptoms of listeria poisoning?
 Listeria poisoning , or listerosis, is a foodborne bacterial infection most commonly caused by the bacterium Listeria monocytogenes, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. It is considered a serious condition and can be dangerous or life-threatening, especially when contracted by adults over 65, people with weak immune systems and pregnant women.
 Symptoms usually start within two weeks of eating contaminated food, but may begin as early as the same day or as late as 10 weeks after. According to the CDC, symptoms include:
 Advertisement Advertisement Fever
 Muscle aches
 Headache
 Stiff neck
 Confusion
 Loss of balance
 Convulsions
 Diarrhea
 Other gastrointestinal symptoms
 Miscarriage, stillbirth, premature delivery and/or life-threatening infection of newborn infants
 Death
 People in higher-risk categories who experience flu-like symptoms within two months of consuming contaminated food should seek medical attention. The CDC estimates about 1,250 people get listeria infections annually in the United States and about 172 people die from the infection.
